source.title: Characterizing Optimizer-Dependent Training Dynamics Through Hessian Eigenvector Displacement and Localization
source.authors: Marcelina Marjankowska; Valerio Modugno; P. Barucca

record.file_problem: None; full paper text is present.
record.tranche_reason: Compares held-out classification performance across optimizers, a different experiment from the benchmark comparisons in V4.
record.gate_note: The study reports optimizer-specific test accuracy in Figure 5 and describes the ranking in Appendix B.2. Hessian displacement, localization, and alignment results do not measure the generalization gap versions describe. The sharpness discussion does not test magnitude-aware sharpness.
record.test_reason: The study directly compares Adam and SGD test accuracy on two image-classification datasets, bearing on V4 under a fixed-learning-rate recipe. Its Hessian dynamics and batch-size ablations do not measure the outcomes required by the other versions.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is accurate. The central conclusion concerns optimizer-dependent Hessian dynamics: SGD progressively stabilizes leading curvature directions, whereas Adam exhibits continued mixing and stronger localization. Robustness has exceptions in full-batch and small-learning-rate regimes. The separately reported test results rank SGD lowest on both datasets, Adam highest on MNIST, and SAM highest on FashionMNIST.
record.recipe_differences: Fixed learning rates and a 3-layer MLP on MNIST and FashionMNIST; no systematic tuning comparison or learning-rate/decay schedule sweep for test accuracy.
record.method_sensitivity: Test-accuracy ranking differs by dataset: Adam is highest on MNIST; SAM is best on FashionMNIST. The reported comparisons use fixed optimizer learning rates.

fits_no_version.finding: SAM exceeds ordinary SGD on both datasets and ranks highest on FashionMNIST.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Sharpness-aware training can improve test accuracy over ordinary SGD in this MLP setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Optimizer-dependent eigenvector displacement, localization and alignment persist across many learning-rate and batch-size settings. Selected solutions also receive eigenvalue and epsilon-sharpness measurements.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Optimizer choice changes Hessian geometry; these measurements do not establish V7's magnitude-aware sharpness versus generalization-gap relationship.

record.peer_reviewed: HiLD 2026: 4th Workshop on High-dimensional Learning Dynamics
record.problems: Test-accuracy values are only plotted in Figure 5, without exact values in the text. The comparison uses one MLP architecture, two datasets, fixed learning rates, and five initializations; it does not test optimizer tuning or directly quantify the training-test gap.
record.rows_left_out: No qualifying results omitted. Hessian displacement, localization, gradient/update alignment, and sharpness observations were not entered because they do not measure the outcomes named by the claim versions.

untested.parts: Random-label memorization and natural-versus-random-label held-out accuracy.
Width-dependent test error beyond the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected networks and the contribution of local connectivity.

Learning-rate or schedule selection for held-out performance; broader tuning; language benchmarks; momentum SGD; decoupled weight decay; switching optimizers; equal-training-performance comparisons. The learning-rate ablation reports geometry rather than test accuracy.
Held-out performance across batch sizes under fixed epoch budgets. The batch-size ablation holds data exposure fixed but reports geometric metrics.
Magnitude-scaled perturbation tolerance, training-test error gaps, and ranking against norm- and margin-based measures within a convolutional family.

missing.what: Figure 4 reports Adam attaining the lowest training loss. Add the corresponding optimizer-by-dataset training-loss comparisons to contextualize its held-out advantage; exact numerical losses are unavailable in the supplied text.

record.verdict_notes: The study is not an original source for these versions. Verdicts rely on the explicit Figure 5 caption ranking, not reconstructed numerical accuracies or significance claims. V4 says adaptive optimizers often generalize worse; these conditional reversals do not refute that frequency claim across benchmarks.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label fitting and held-out accuracy on natural versus random labels.
Width sweep past the zero-training-error threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected architecture comparisons.
Language benchmarks; broader hyperparameter tuning; decoupled weight decay; switching from Adam to SGD; effects of optimizer choice on the training-test gap itself.
Large-batch effects on held-out performance under fixed epoch budgets.
Magnitude-aware perturbation sharpness and comparison against norm- and margin-based measures.
Removing memorized training examples and measuring test accuracy.
